answer: Like light through a prism, an agent economy can split every newcomer's stake from its earnings: each identity locks a refundable deposit before it may trade. A bridge between markets and courts, a rotating jury of established agents, inspects suspicious work, and if fraud is proven the deposit is slashed and paid to the honest. A lotus grows only from clean mud: a fake army needs a fresh deposit for every identity, and each caught fake burns real money, so flooding the economy costs far more than it can ever earn.
